# Australian accounting engines and MCP server

> Seven independently released Python engines that apply Australian tax and payroll
> rules to figures you supply, plus Aus Accounting MCP, a local Model Context Protocol
> server that hands those engines to an AI assistant. The engines and the server run
> locally, contact no service, write to no ledger and lodge nothing. A person reviews
> every output before it is relied on.

Ryan Duguid is not a registered tax agent or BAS agent. Fixtures and examples are
fabricated. Nothing here is tax, legal or financial advice. An MCP host sends every
tool argument and result to its model provider.

## Start

- [README](https://github.com/ryanduguid/australian-accounting#readme): what each component does, a one-contribution Payday Super trial and the evidence boundary.
- [Scope, limits and examples](https://duguid.com.au/tools/australian-tax-ai-agents/): the maintained guide to the MCP server, its install commands, supported periods and refusals.
- [MCP client setup](https://github.com/ryanduguid/australian-accounting/blob/main/apps/aus-accounting-mcp/README.md#client-integration): run `uvx aus-accounting-mcp` as a local stdio server. It needs Python 3.11 or later and no API key. Official MCP registry name: io.github.ryanduguid/aus-accounting.
- [Tool reference](https://github.com/ryanduguid/australian-accounting/blob/main/apps/aus-accounting-mcp/README.md#tools): every MCP tool, its inputs and what it refuses.

## Components

Each component keeps its own distribution, version, release notes, tests and `CITATION.cff`, and is released on the tag `<component>/vX.Y.Z`.

- [aus-accounting-mcp](https://github.com/ryanduguid/australian-accounting/tree/main/apps/aus-accounting-mcp): the MCP server.
- [payday-super-checker](https://github.com/ryanduguid/australian-accounting/tree/main/packages/payday-super-checker): Payday Super contribution timing review from supplied payroll and fund-receipt evidence.
- [ato-benchmark-compare](https://github.com/ryanduguid/australian-accounting/tree/main/packages/ato-benchmark-compare): ATO small business benchmark ratio comparison.
- [div7a-loan-review](https://github.com/ryanduguid/australian-accounting/tree/main/packages/div7a-loan-review): experimental Division 7A loan-term and minimum yearly repayment review. Not a Division 7A determination.
- [australian-tax-calculators](https://github.com/ryanduguid/australian-accounting/tree/main/packages/australian-tax-calculators): bounded Australian tax calculation worksheets with explicit scope and sources.
- [the-exchequer-tally](https://github.com/ryanduguid/australian-accounting/tree/main/packages/the-exchequer-tally): company tax rate, franking account and Division 203 benchmark rule checks.
- [solomons-sword](https://github.com/ryanduguid/australian-accounting/tree/main/packages/solomons-sword): trust distribution allocation and Division 6, section 100A and section 99B review checks.
- [the-wip-tally](https://github.com/ryanduguid/australian-accounting/tree/main/packages/the-wip-tally): a deterministic AASB 15 construction WIP schedule.
- [au-tax-rates-data](https://github.com/ryanduguid/australian-accounting/tree/main/packages/au-tax-rates-data): key ATO rates and thresholds with verbatim source quotes and a validator. Never released.
